headline: Red Sox crush Diamondbacks as every starter joins the party
morning_brew: That is exactly how you answer a gutless weekend on the road. The Red Sox put a real hurting on the Diamondbacks last night at Fenway Park, scoring in such bunches that the scoreboard operator practically needed a break. It was a complete team effort, with every single guy in the starting lineup driving in a run, and watching us pile up hits made those last few days of pure frustration feel like a distant, bad dream.

Gamboa only went a short stretch, but the bullpen finally decided to stop acting like the arson squad and kept Arizona under wraps. Bello was the absolute workhorse, coming in to eat up a massive chunk of the middle innings and shutting things down with authority. I haven't seen a lineup clicking like that since before the mid-summer dog days, and it feels like this team is finally playing with the kind of desperate urgency we expected back in April.

My neighbor Rick is already busy obsessing over the challenge system tracker for the next few days, but I am just enjoying the fact that for one night, I didn't have to watch the game through my fingers like I was witnessing a crime. We have the next few nights to keep this momentum going right here at home, and if the bats stay this hot, we might actually make this wild card race interesting. I am not gonna get ahead of myself, but it was a damn fine night to be at the oldest yard in baseball.
